title: Hosted Rollouts (GA) — Policy validation rules + beta→v2 migration notes
content:
Context
- This doc captures working notes for rollout_policy v2 validation in control plane (Hosted canary GA).
- Focus: percent sum constraints, guardrail requirements, entitlements/RBAC gating, and beta schema migration.
- Primary consumers: policy engine + control plane API layer + Console surface (error messaging).

Non-goals / out of scope for now
- Statistical methods for quality gates (handled by eval/quality systems).
- Data-plane routing implementation details (weights application, sticky routing semantics).

Key objectives for validation
1) Prevent unsafe misconfigurations (e.g., 100% candidate w/ no guardrails) and reduce incidents.
2) Keep policy evaluation deterministic under high QPS.
3) Support backwards-compatible reads from beta while enforcing GA rules on writes.
4) Produce actionable error messages for Console.

Terminology (internal)
- Baseline: current production model/version.
- Candidate: new model/version being rolled out.
- Variant: baseline or candidate.
- Step/schedule: how traffic weights change over time (manual steps or timed progression).
- Guardrails: automated stop/rollback triggers based on telemetry and/or quality gates.
- Effective routing: resolved weights after applying policy layers (account/route/region) + schedule state.

Validation surfaces
A) Policy write validation (create/update) — strict.
B) Policy read/normalize (loading existing persisted policies) — tolerant + emits warnings.
C) Policy evaluation time checks — MUST be deterministic; no network calls.


I. Percent / weight constraints

Weights shape
- GA supports 2-variant rollouts for Hosted: baseline + candidate.
- Future: multi-variant A/B/n; we should design v2 constraints to extend cleanly.

Rules (write-time)
1) Sum-to-100 invariant
- For each step that specifies weights: sum(weights) must equal 100.
- Accept integers only (0–100) for now.
  - Reason: routing engine uses integer weights; simplifies determinism + UI.
- If step omitted weights, derive from previous step (see schedule rules).

2) Range checks
- Each weight must be 0..100 inclusive.
- baseline_weight == 0 is allowed only if additional safety conditions met (see guardrails).

3) Candidate extremes
- candidate_weight == 100 is allowed only if:
  a) user has explicit permission (see entitlements/RBAC), AND
  b) at least one “hard” guardrail configured (latency or error-rate), OR an explicit override flag acknowledged in Console (product decision pending), AND
  c) rollout is not in "in_progress" timed progression state (i.e., setting 100% should effectively complete/pin).
- candidate_weight == 0 is always allowed (equivalent to pausing at 0% candidate; still keep policy around).

4) Step monotonicity (timed schedules)
- For timed progression schedules, enforce non-decreasing candidate weight across steps (monotonic up).
  - Allows repeats (e.g., 10,10,25) but not decreases.
  - If we want “ramp down” that should be pause/rollback, not schedule.
- For manual schedules, allow arbitrary changes (but still validated by guardrails + permissions).

5) Step count constraints
- Min steps: 1.
- Max steps: propose 20 (open: align with Console UI limits).
- Timed schedules: each step must include a duration_seconds (or start_at) with a minimum granularity (>= 60s).

6) Schedule state constraints
- Only one active schedule per policy.
- If schedule is “timed progression,” require a start_time and a current_step pointer OR derive based on monotonic version + elapsed time. Prefer explicit persisted state to avoid time drift across regions.

Normalization (read-time)
- If a beta policy has decimal weights, round using "largest remainder" method to preserve sum=100.
- If sum != 100 due to historical bugs, normalize by scaling, record warning event, and clamp at 0..100.

Error messaging guidance
- Prefer pointing to the exact step index and field: steps[3].weights.candidate.
- Provide "expected sum = 100" messages and current computed sum.


II. Guardrail requirements

Guardrail taxonomy (current)
- Telemetry-based guardrails:
  - error_rate_threshold (e.g., candidate 5xx > baseline + X% OR absolute > Y%)
  - latency_threshold (p95 or p99) deltas, absolute threshold, and/or budget.
  - token_cost_delta_threshold (candidate cost per 1k tokens > baseline * (1+delta))
- Optional quality gates:
  - eval_regression_threshold referencing a named eval suite / prompt set (async system).

GA safety stance (proposal)
- At least one telemetry-based guardrail REQUIRED for any rollout that ever sets candidate_weight > 0.
  - Rationale: quality gates are not always configured/available; telemetry is universal.
- Additionally, for candidate_weight >= 50 in any step, require:
  - BOTH error-rate + latency guardrails, unless user has "rollouts.guardrails.override" permission.
  - Open question: do we require both at 25%+ instead?

Constraints on thresholds
- Threshold fields must be within sane ranges to prevent "always pass" configs.
  - Example:
    - error_rate_abs must be between 0.1% and 20% (configurable server-side).
    - latency_delta_ms must be between 10ms and 5000ms.
    - cost_delta_pct must be between 1% and 200%.
- Guardrail evaluation windows must be chosen from a limited set (e.g., 1m, 5m, 15m) to control cardinality and avoid arbitrary windowing.

“Guardrail required” edge cases
- If candidate_weight == 0 for all steps (i.e., rollout created but not started), guardrails may be omitted.
- If rollout is created at candidate_weight > 0 (Console might allow start-at-1%), enforce guardrails at creation.

Defaults
- Console should pre-fill defaults; control plane must not rely on client.
- Proposed server-side defaults (if omitted but allowed):
  - error_rate_guardrail: enabled with conservative threshold
  - latency_guardrail: enabled with conservative delta
- BUT: there’s a product tension here. If we auto-add guardrails silently, users may be surprised. Prefer: server rejects if missing; Console provides a one-click “add recommended guardrails.”

Guardrail evaluation determinism
- Policy engine should only validate schema + config. Runtime guardrail checking happens via monitoring/automation system.
- For validation, ensure that guardrails reference only supported metric names + aggregation keys; no arbitrary PromQL.


III. Entitlements + RBAC gating

Entitlements (plan-level)
- Feature gated by plan: Hosted rollouts GA.
- Entitlement checks at write-time:
  - Creating a rollout policy requires "hosted_rollouts" entitlement.
  - Editing weights requires entitlement + RBAC permission.
  - Pause/rollback endpoints also require permissions.

RBAC permissions (action-level)
- Proposed permission set (names approximate; align with rbac-policy-bundle):
  - rollouts.create
  - rollouts.update
  - rollouts.pause
  - rollouts.rollback
  - rollouts.override_safety (allows risky actions like 100% candidate without full guardrails)

Role mapping notes
- Admin can do all.
- Developer can create/update but cannot override safety (no 100% candidate, cannot remove guardrails once active).
- Read-only can view effective routing and audit history only.

Validation interactions with RBAC
- Validation needs actor context (who is making change) because some configs are only allowed with override.
- Implementation: validation function signature includes (policy, actor, account_entitlements, current_policy_state).

State-aware permissions
- If rollout is "active" (candidate_weight > 0), tightening rules:
  - Cannot remove all guardrails.
  - Cannot change baseline target without rollback first (see invariants below).

Console expectations
- Provide structured errors:
  - code: PERMISSION_DENIED, ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED, VALIDATION_FAILED
  - field_errors: list with pointer + message


IV. Policy invariants (important for safety)

1) Baseline immutability during active rollout
- Once candidate traffic > 0, baseline target (model/version) must not change.
  - Reason: comparison is against baseline; changing baseline invalidates guardrails + metrics.
- Candidate target can change only when candidate_weight == 0 (or require rollback + new rollout).
  - Open: allow candidate retargeting at 0% only (safe).

2) Route binding
- Policy must reference a stable route_id.
- If route is deleted/disabled:
  - control plane should reject future updates; keep policy for audit but mark as "orphaned".

3) Region scoping
- For Hosted, rollout policy is route-scoped and applies across regions.
- If we ever support per-region rollouts, policy schema needs explicit region overrides; until then, reject region-specific weights in v2.

4) Sticky routing config (if present)
- stickiness must be one of: none | request_hash | session (naming TBD).
- If stickiness == session, require session_id source configured.
- For now, if stickiness enabled, require deterministic hash key definition and documented fallback if missing.


V. Beta → v2 migration strategy

What exists in beta (summary)
- Beta rollout config stored with older field names and sometimes only a single "candidatePercent" field.
- Some policies may not have explicit guardrails; beta relied on human monitoring.

Principles
- Backwards-compatible reads: continue to load beta policies and render in Console.
- Strict GA writes: any create/update via v2 endpoints must satisfy v2 validation.
- Avoid surprise behavior changes: do not silently ramp traffic differently.

Proposed migration plan
Phase 1: Read compatibility layer
- On read:
  - Detect schema version.
  - Convert beta -> v2 normalized internal representation.
  - Emit warning log + metric: rollout_policy_migration_warning{reason=...}.

Phase 2: Dual-write (optional)
- If needed for rollback: write v2, also store a beta shadow record.
- Prefer not to dual-write long-term.

Phase 3: Backfill job
- Background job to convert stored beta policies to v2 persisted form.
- Backfill should NOT add guardrails automatically; instead mark policy as "needs_guardrails" and restrict edits until guardrails are added.
  - Note: product decision: do we allow “grandfathered” beta rollouts to continue without guardrails? Recommendation: allow read-only + pause/rollback, but block increasing candidate% until guardrails set.

Grandfathering rules (recommended)
- Existing beta rollouts:
  - Allowed actions without adding guardrails:
    - pause to 0%
    - rollback to baseline 100%
    - view
  - Disallowed actions:
    - increase candidate%
    - set candidate to 100%
    - add timed progression
- Rationale: keeps customers safe without breaking ability to mitigate.

Data model mapping notes
- beta.candidatePercent -> v2.steps[0].weights.candidate
- baseline weight = 100 - candidatePercent
- if beta had "startAt"/"endAt" schedule, map to timed progression steps; if ambiguous, map to manual single-step and mark schedule_unmigrated.

Audit implications
- Migration/backfill must generate audit events with actor="system" and include before/after.
- Ensure audit payload doesn’t include full prompts or PII.


VI. Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm product stance on requiring BOTH error+latency guardrails at 50%+.
- Decide maximum steps and minimum duration for timed progression.
- Finalize which fields are “editable while active” vs “must pause first.”
- Determine if we allow 100% candidate without guardrails for internal/dev accounts (feature flag / internal entitlement).
- Confirm whether cost guardrail is required for certain plans (enterprise asks).


VII. Proposed tests (validation unit tests)
- weights sum != 100 -> reject with field pointer.
- candidate=100 w/o override -> reject.
- candidate increases with timed schedule but guardrails missing -> reject.
- timed schedule with decreasing candidate -> reject.
- active rollout baseline change -> reject.
- beta policy read with decimal weights -> normalize and warn.
- beta policy update attempt to increase candidate without guardrails -> reject with actionable message.


VIII. Notes from Slack (for context)
- Policy schema thread consensus: keep v2 strict and deterministic; do not allow arbitrary scripts/queries in guardrails.
- RBAC thread: ensure Console can show “why denied” (entitlement vs permission) and provide admin remediation text.

Appendix: Example error messages (copy for API)
- "steps[2].weights: weights must sum to 100; got 95"
- "guardrails: at least one telemetry guardrail is required when candidate_weight > 0"
- "permissions: rollouts.override_safety required to set candidate_weight to 100"
- "baseline: cannot change baseline target while rollout is active (candidate_weight > 0)"
